main_text.p: inquit vobiscum sum, omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem sæculi.] Et in Epistola ad Cyriacum, eadem eiusdem constantiæ pariter & obedientiæ elucet, [cum à ciuitate inquit fugarer,dicebam intra meipsum: si quidem vult Regina me exulem agere, agat in exilium: Domini est terra & plenitudo eius: Et si vult secare, secet, idem passus est Isaias[?]: si vult in pelagus me mittere, Jona recordabor; si vult in caminum inijcere, idem passi sunt tres illi Pueri: si me foris vult obijcere, obijciat; Danielis in lacum Leonibus obiecti reminiscar: si me lapidare vult, lapidet; socium habeo Stephanum Proto-Martyrem: & si caput tollere vult, tollat; habeo socium Johannem Baptistam: & si substantiam auferre, auferat; nudus exiui ex utero matris meæ, nudus etiam reuertar.] Vox herclę digna, & fideli subdito, & infracto Præsule, neq; alia illi post reditu mens. [Dicite mihi, inquit, quomodo persequuti estis Lupos? quomodo pepuliftis Patrono? frequenti scilicet oratione ad Deũ, quomodo despexistis adulteros ? continuis lachrymis ex desiderio viri.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "Ifaias" (printed with a long-s-like form, read as Isaias, marked [?]). Long s rendered as plain s throughout ("si", "secare", "substantiam"), where the printed form resembles f. The initial I of Iona and Iohannem is read as J per the consonant rule; the printed form is I. The opening fragment "inquit vobiscum sum" begins mid-paragraph. No indented paragraph breaks are visible, so the page is one paragraph.
